sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in North Carolina, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 20Passed

Your county board of elections had to receive your request by 5 p.m. two Tuesdays before Election Day: Tuesday, October 20, 2026. That deadline has passed. You can still vote early in person through 3 p.m. Saturday, October 31 (and register at the same time if you are not registered in your county), or vote at your polling place on Election Day. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must reach your county board of elections by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, whether or not it has a postmark. State law used to count ballots postmarked by Election Day that came within three days; that is no longer the case. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Saturday, October 31, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on North Carolina’s own site

At school away from home, in North Carolina or in another state? What North Carolina says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. Any registered North Carolina voter may ask for, receive and vote a mail-in absentee ballot. You must ask for one each election; ballots are not mailed to everyone. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Use the State Board of Elections' NC Absentee Ballot Portal (Option 1). You need your date of birth and your North Carolina driver's license or DMV ID number, or the last four digits of your Social Security number. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Fill out the official 2026 NC Absentee Ballot Request Form, sign it by hand (a typed signature is not allowed), and send it to your county board of elections by the U.S. Postal Service, DHL, FedEx or UPS. You, a near relative or your legal guardian must sign it. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Hand the signed paper request form in at your county board of elections office. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Put correct postage on the return envelope: $1.98 for the 2026 general election (three Forever stamps cover it). It must arrive by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)
  • In person. Hand it to your county board of elections office (by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day), or to an election official at any early voting site in your county while it is open (early voting ends 3 p.m. Saturday, October 31). You may NOT turn it in at a polling place on Election Day. Only you, your near relative (spouse, brother, sister, parent, child, stepchild, grandparent, grandchild, stepparent, or a parent-, son- or daughter-in-law) or your legal guardian may mail or deliver it; a voter who needs help because of a disability may ask anyone. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Mark your ballot in front of two witnesses or one notary. They watch that you mark it, not how you vote. Anyone 18 or older can be a witness, except (with a few exceptions) a candidate. You sign the envelope; each witness signs, prints their name and writes their full address on it. Put a copy of an accepted photo ID in the clear sleeve on the back of the envelope; if you cannot, fill out the yellow Photo ID Exception form from your ballot package and put it in the sleeve instead. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on North Carolina’s own site

Sign up for BallotTrax to follow your ballot from printed to accepted. (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Thursday, October 15, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Early voting in person runs from Thursday, October 15 to 3 p.m. Saturday, October 31, 2026, at any early voting site in your county. If you are not registered in that county you can register and vote at the same visit (same-day registration), bringing proof of where you live. (official page)

Students

At school in North Carolina, away from home

The State Board says college and university students may register and vote in the county where they live while at school if they do not plan to return to their former home after graduating. A student who does not know where they will go after college may register either in their college community or at their former home. A student who plans to return home after graduating should be registered there. During early voting a student can register at an early voting site in the college's county and vote right away, bringing proof of address; a student living on campus can use a school document showing their campus housing address. You may vote only once in any election. (official page)

At school in another state, with North Carolina as home

The State Board's rule for students is the same: if you plan to return to your North Carolina home after graduating, you should stay registered there. On the absentee request form you can give a different address where your ballot should be mailed, such as your school address out of state. Voting more than once in the same election, in North Carolina or across state lines, is a felony. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military and overseas voters have later deadlines: register and request by 5 p.m. Monday, November 2, 2026. A ballot sent back by email, online or fax must arrive by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day; a mailed ballot counts if it was sent by 12:01 a.m. on Election Day where you voted it and arrives by 5 p.m. Thursday, November 12, 2026. A photo ID rule applies to state and local offices; see the instructions in your ballot package. (federal guide)

North Carolina in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The deadline to ask for a mail ballot (5 p.m. Tuesday, October 20, 2026) has passed for most voters. If you already have a ballot, return it so it arrives by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day; mail it soon or hand it in at an early voting site in your county.
  • Blind and visually impaired voters can ask for, mark and return an accessible absentee ballot online, with a typed or digital signature.
  • Voters in a hospital, clinic, nursing home or adult care home can ask their county board for a Multipartisan Assistance Team.
  • Polls on Election Day are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., and you must vote at your assigned polling place.
